# Laboratory exception review


The workspace edits persistent documents and submits snapshots to a review queue.
The public API is synchronous: open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), dispose().
Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text.
The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval; hiding it
cancels unpublished work and later queries remain usable.

The coordinator owns editor visits; the acquired confirmation capability owns a view outlet. The document repository and durable queue are separate services. Component or native source defines the local service contracts.
Their local interface contracts define the behavior to preserve.

The injected store has read/write/subscribe, the queue has enqueue/list/subscribe,
and timers have schedule(callback, delay)/cancel(handle). Render functions are
output sinks and do not call application code. Keep the workspace API and these
injected interfaces. A submission returns the queue receipt, or null when no
editor is selected. Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace.

Vue3 Composition API shallowRef owns visit identity; onBeforeUnmount closes while durable queue remains outside reactive view state.

An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity. Native RPC only adapts timer and passive output/integration resource calls; storage, queue delivery, acquired outlet and command state execute in the target runtime.

<template><section><textarea :value="visit ? visit.text : ''" @input="edit($event.target.value)"></textarea><button @click="submit">Accept worksheet</button></section></template>
<script>
import {shallowRef, onBeforeUnmount} from 'vue3';
import {trailing,bindConfirmation} from './services.js';
export default {
  props: ['services'],
  setup(props) {
    const visit=shallowRef(null);
    const api={env: props.services, navigation: 0, getVisit: ()=>visit.value, setVisit: value=>{visit.value=value;},
retire() {
  const leaving = this.getVisit();
  if (leaving) {
    leaving.task.flush();
    leaving.stop();
  }
  this.setVisit(null);
  this.env.renderDocument(null);
  
},
open(id) {
  this.env.renderSubmission(null);
  const request = ++this.navigation;
  this.retire();
  
  const stop = this.env.store.subscribe(event => { if (event.id === id) this.env.renderStatus(event); });
  const task = trailing(this.env.timers, 120, text => this.env.store.write(id, text));
  const visit = {id, text: this.env.store.read(id), stop, task};
  this.setVisit(visit); this.env.renderDocument({id, text: visit.text});
},
edit(text) {
  const visit = this.getVisit(); if (!visit) return;
  visit.text = text;
  visit.task.push(text);
},
close() { this.env.renderSubmission(null); ++this.navigation; this.retire(); },
submit() {
  const confirmation=bindConfirmation(()=>this.getVisit(),receipt=>this.env.renderSubmission(receipt));
  const visit = this.getVisit(); if (!visit) return null;
  const snapshot = {id: visit.id, text: visit.text};
  visit.task.flush();
  const receipt = this.env.archive.capture(snapshot);
  
  confirmation.show(receipt);
  return receipt;
},

    };
    onBeforeUnmount(()=>api.close());
    return {visit,open: id=>api.open(id),edit: text=>api.edit(text),close: ()=>api.close(),submit: ()=>api.submit()};
  },
};
</script>

checkpoints: After one or more edits, no store write occurs until the 120 ms quiet interval expires.
At the quiet interval, exactly the latest text from that burst is written for the originating document.
After a burst saves, a later edit burst schedules and completes another save.
Before open, close, submission, or component teardown retires the current visit, its accepted pending text is settled so it is not lost.

Submission archives the current visit's latest text and returns the archive receipt synchronously; confirmation is emitted only if the visit acquired by the outlet is still active after archive callbacks.
Opening or closing a visit still removes its store subscription, and search-preview behavior remains unchanged.
forbidden_effects: Do not continue writing on every keystroke.
Do not write intermediate texts from the same uninterrupted editing burst.
Do not discard an accepted pending edit when opening another document, closing, submitting, or unmounting.
Do not let a timer owned by a retired visit write again after that visit's pending value has already been settled.
Do not attribute an old visit's pending save, receipt, status, or confirmation to a newly opened visit, including a reopening of the same document id.
Do not show a confirmation for the originating visit if a synchronous archive listener navigates away during capture.
Do not change the synchronous public API or the injected store, archive, timer, rendering, and confirmation interfaces.
Do not modify the adjacent 40 ms search-preview policy.
lifecycle_identity: Each call to open creates a fresh editor visit identity, even when reopening the same document id.
The trailing edit task belongs to the visit and document id for which it was created; document-id equality alone is not sufficient to identify the active visit.
The confirmation outlet owns the exact visit active when bindConfirmation is called and may publish only while that same object remains current.
Archive receipts retain the captured snapshot's document id and text independently of later navigation or editing.

obligations.text: edit(text) must synchronously update the selected visit's in-memory text but coalesce persistence through that visit's existing trailing task, using a 120 ms quiet interval.
For each uninterrupted editing burst, persistence must write only the latest text once after the quiet interval; once that execution is consumed, later bursts must be schedulable and save normally.

A pending accepted edit must be settled before lifecycle operations retire its visit or depend on its persisted value, including switching documents, close/unmount, and submission; settling must consume or cancel the scheduled execution so it cannot later duplicate the write.
Visit retirement must continue detaching the visit's store subscription and clearing the document rendering, without allowing the old visit's work to affect a replacement visit.
submit() must remain synchronous, return null when no visit is selected, otherwise archive and return a receipt for the originating visit's latest {id, text} snapshot.

Submission confirmation must remain bound to the visit active at outlet acquisition and must recheck that exact visit after archive.capture returns, because archive listeners can synchronously navigate.
The existing open, edit, close, submit, and teardown surfaces and all injected service interfaces must be preserved; the 40 ms search preview is outside the change.

ordering_barriers: Within edit, update visit.text before scheduling its trailing persistence so submission can snapshot the latest accepted text synchronously.
At a 120 ms timer callback, consume the captured latest burst value and clear that scheduled execution before permitting a later burst to schedule independently.
Settle a visit's pending edit before its subscription is detached and before the visit is discarded, so accepted text and its existing synchronous store notification behavior are not silently lost.

During submit, acquire confirmation ownership and capture the originating visit and latest snapshot before any callback-capable boundary; settle its pending store write before archive.capture(snapshot).
Call confirmation.show(receipt) only after archive.capture(snapshot) returns, so the outlet's identity check observes navigation performed by archive listeners.
On component teardown, perform the documented close behavior while leaving the durable archive outside reactive view state.
preservation: Keep open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), and disposal behavior synchronous.
Keep open restoring text from store.read(id), creating a new visit, subscribing to store status, and rendering the opened document.
Keep store notifications and revisions produced through store.write; coalescing changes their frequency only as required by TASK.
Keep submit returning the archive receipt, or null with no selected editor.
Keep archive capture durable and independent of reactive visit state.
Keep confirmation publication scoped to the exact visit acquired by bindConfirmation.
Keep document and submission clearing behavior on navigation and close.
Keep search preview trailing publication at 40 ms, with hide cancelling unpublished work and later queries remaining usable.

diagnoses.explanation: The behavioral contract does not need revision. The candidate correctly replaces per-keystroke persistence with visit.task.push(text), and the public trailing utility already retires its ticket before consuming a value, allowing subsequent bursts. However, the candidate never flushes or cancels that task when a visit is retired and never flushes it before submission. Consequently, an accepted edit can be lost at a lifecycle boundary or can write later from a retired visit; submission can archive the latest in-memory text while its corresponding store write remains pending. These violate preservation and lifecycle obligations already grounded in the original synchronous behavior. The candidate's bindConfirmation usage does preserve exact-visit checking after synchronous archive listeners run.

The public documents do not describe a separate host-level dispose mapping beyond onBeforeUnmount calling close().

routing_analysis.contract: A selected editor visit owns its 120 ms trailing persistence task. edit updates that visit's in-memory text immediately and pushes the latest text into the task; an uninterrupted burst produces one store write after quiet, and the task must remain reusable for later bursts. Before open, close/unmount, or submit crosses a lifecycle boundary, accepted pending text must be settled without leaving a duplicate retired-visit timer. Submission remains synchronous: bind confirmation to the originating visit, snapshot its latest text, settle persistence, call archive.capture, and publish only if that exact visit remains current after synchronous archive listeners. Store subscriptions, rendering, fresh visit identity, return values, injected interfaces, and the separate 40 ms search preview remain preserved.
